statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered using Latin alphabet characters and numerals; te reo Māori names with macrons are accepted. Non-Latin script names require a romanized transliteration for the statutory register. The name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing New Zealand registered name, reserved name, or overseas registered name protected in New Zealand.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation in New Zealand is valid for 20 working days and cannot be extended. If incorporation is not completed within that period, the reservation lapses and a fresh application and fee must be submitted. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the New Zealand Companies Office setting out the statutory grounds and supporting evidence. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant may seek judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable as a registered office address for a New Zealand company provided it is a physical street address in New Zealand and not a post-office box, and the service provider is engaged as registered agent to receive and forward legal and government documents. For an AIGC software and virtual avatar generation SaaS business, a virtual office does not by itself create New Zealand tax residence where central management and control remain outside New Zealand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated under 5%): unannounced physical inspections are uncommon for an unlicensed software/SaaS company absent a substantiated complaint, AML/CFT risk trigger, or Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment compliance audit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), principally ss 10 (no minimum capital), 15 (company capacity), 20 (application for registration), 21 (registration and certificate of incorporation), 28 (default constitution), 31 (registered office), 32 (address for service), 42–43 (solvency test for share allotment), 110 (allotment of shares), 122 (appointment of directors), 126 (consent to act as director), 153 (board resolution and records), 157–161 (directors' duties), 199–200 (audit exemption for small companies), 214 (annual return); together with the Companies (Fees) Regulations 2013 (incorporation fee NZ$150) and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (private company exempt issuer status).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ngā Kōreti Umanga), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), operating the online Companies Register portal at www.companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz, Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form: 'Apply to Incorporate a Company' (electronic application filed through the New Zealand Companies Register); official instrument issued: 'Certificate of Incorporation' pursuant to s 21(3) of the Companies Act 1993, together with the automatically allocated New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorized, issued, or paid-up share capital applies to a New Zealand company under the Companies Act 1993 (s 10 abolishes the concept of authorized capital). Shares may be allotted for nil or nominal consideration without escrow, deposit, or capitalization account requirements. The operative statutory constraint is solvency-based: under ss 42–43, directors must believe on reasonable grounds that the company will satisfy the solvency test immediately after each share allotment. For the CK_IC entity, the international company classification imposes no separate capital benchmark.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [THE INTERNATIONAL COMPANY] (CK_IC), A NEW ZEALAND LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY REGISTERED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT 1993. ADOPTED IN WRITING AND RECORDED PURSUANT TO ss 122 AND 153 OF THE COMPANIES ACT 1993.

RESOLVED:

1. INCORPORATION RATIFICATION: That the application for registration filed with the New Zealand Companies Office under s 20 of the Companies Act 1993 be and is hereby ratified, and that the Certificate of Incorporation issued under s 21(3), together with the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), be accepted, filed in the statutory records, and recorded in the minutes of this meeting.

2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: That the share capital of the Company be fixed at 1,000 ordinary shares of NZ$0.01 each, par value NZ$10.00 in aggregate; that the subscriptions tendered by the founding shareholders, as set out in the incorporation application, be and are hereby approved; and that the allotment of shares be effected in accordance with ss 42–43 and s 110 of the Companies Act 1993, with the directors confirming the solvency test is satisfied immediately following allotment. Share certificates shall be issued under the common seal, if any, or under director signature.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company, as notified to the New Zealand Companies Office under s 31 of the Companies Act 1993, be and is hereby fixed at the address recorded in the Companies Register, being the physical place where the statutory register is kept during business hours, and that the agent named on the register be authorized to accept service of legal process under s 32.

4. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Sole Director of the Company to hold office in accordance with the Constitution and ss 122 and 126 of the Companies Act 1993; that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary (optional office) with authority to execute all administrative filings; and that the managing director or delegated officer be authorized to open and operate banking accounts and payment-rail accounts (including Stripe and Paddle) for the Company's AIGC video-generation SaaS business.

5. AUDIT WAIVER: That the appointment of an auditor be and is hereby waived for the current financial year pursuant to s 200 of the Companies Act 1993, the Company being a small company exempt from audit on the grounds that it has not had more than 50 shareholders and does not meet the FMC reporting entity thresholds.

6. REVENUE AND TAX DIRECTIVES: That the officers be and are hereby instructed to register the Company with Inland Revenue for an IRD number, to consider GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 (compulsory where NZ taxable turnover exceeds NZ$60,000 in any 12-month period), and to maintain all books, records, and tax filings in compliance with the Tax Administration Act 1994 and Financial Reporting Act 2013.

7. GOVERNANCE AND OPERATIONS: That the Company adopt a written minute book, share register, director register, and registered office register; that the Company's business scope be deemed to include software development, AI video synthesis, virtual avatar generation, SaaS distribution, and related licensing; and that the directors be authorized to execute all contracts, NDAs, and terms of service necessary for the commercial launch.

DATED this ______ day of __________________, 20______.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register online portal (www.companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name availability search against the register of legal entity names. The proposed name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing name and must not contravene s 22 of the Companies Act 1993 (no misleading, offensive, or restricted words). If a name is available, the applicant may reserve it for 20 working days pending filing of the incorporation application; reservation is optional but recommended to secure the name.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and alternative name (if applicable)
Statement of intended business scope (ISIC 6201 / AI video synthesis SaaS)
Name reservation reference number (if online reservation used)
Consent of prospective directors to act under s 126 (prepared in draft)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the Companies Office will issue a provisional refusal notice; the applicant may submit a new name for search, or apply for a name review through the Companies Office customer service channel, and may file the incorporation application using the alternative reserved name without restarting the substantive process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution, Director Consents, and Registered Office Designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (pre-filing preparation by legal counsel; no filing fee at this step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the company constitution, either adopting the default constitution under s 28 of the Companies Act 1993 or a bespoke constitution tailored to the international SaaS structure (including non-resident ownership rights and share transfer restrictions). Secure each director's signed consent to act under s 126, confirm the proposed registered office is a physical address in New Zealand at which the register will be kept under s 31, and record the address for service under s 32.
required_dossiers: Constitution (executed by subscribers) or notation adopting the statutory default under s 28
Consent to act as director (Form 8 or equivalent) executed by each proposed director
Notice of registered office physical address in New Zealand
Address for service in New Zealand
Schedule of initial share allotments and subscriber names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries any consent or address at filing, the applicant has 15 working days to respond with corrective documents; defective consents are simply re-executed and re-uploaded and the application is resubmitted without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — Companies Register online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic application for incorporation under s 20 of the Companies Act 1993 via the Companies Register. Complete all director, shareholder, registered office, and share structure fields. Certify that each director is eligible (natural person, 18 years or older, not disqualified under ss 151–152). Pay the statutory filing fee of NZ$150 (approximately US$90) by debit or credit card immediately upon submission. The system requires the application to be digitally signed or verified by the applicant; each director must indicate consent within the portal.
required_dossiers: Completed online incorporation application (s 20 Companies Act 1993)
Constitution (uploaded, if bespoke; otherwise default terms are recorded)
Consent to act for each director (uploaded as executed)
Notice of registered office address
Proof of payment of the NZ$150 filing fee
Subscriber identification details (full legal name, date of birth, residential address)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office issues a defect notice or inquiry, the applicant must respond within 15 working days through the Companies Register correspondence function, filing amended consents or corrected registered-office details. If the application is rejected, it may be re-filed with the corrected data; the statutory fee is retained only where a certificate has already issued, and fee relief may be requested in cases of registry error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Companies Register automatically issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation under s 21(3) of the Companies Act 1993 and allocates the NZBN. The certificate records the company name, registration number, date of incorporation, and entity type (New Zealand limited liability company). The incorporator should download and archive the certificate, register the company in the NZBN directory, and include the NZBN in all business correspondence and invoicing.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation (issued by Companies Office)
New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) auto-generated registration record
Internal incorporation checklist signed by the founding director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a clerical error (e.g., misspelled name or incorrect share class description), the director may apply to the Companies Office for administrative correction under s 21(4) and for re-issuance of the certificate; same-process corrections are normally completed within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: IRD Registration, GST Election, and Tax Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue (IRD) — New Zealand Business registration via the Inland Revenue portal or through the Companies Register integrated 'Start a Business' function
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for an Inland Revenue Department (IRD) number using the company's NZBN and certificate of incorporation, either online via the business registration tool or by paper form. Assess GST registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985: registration is mandatory where taxable supplies exceed NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period; voluntary registration is permissible at the formation stage to recover input VAT on launch costs. Appoint a tax agent or nominate the CFO as the company's contact person for tax correspondence. If the company will have contracted staff or employees, register as an employer for PAYE and KiwiSaver obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Directors' and shareholders' identification documents (IRD requires NZ IRD numbers or equivalent foreign tax identification numbers)
Registered office and address for service confirmation
GST registration form (online) or IRD business registration form IR596
Banking details of the company for refund processing
Company business activity description (AI video synthesis and virtual avatar generation software; ISIC 6201)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRD registration is held for identity verification, the company should escalate through the IRD Business contact line (0800 377 774) or via the secure myIR business mailbox; outstanding identification documents may be submitted digitally and the registration will be backdated to the date of original application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Bank Account, and Payment Rail Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; registered office agent; commercial banks in New Zealand (e.g., ANZ, ASB, BNZ, Westpac) and payment service providers (Stripe, Paddle)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or pass a written resolution under s 153) adopting the pro forma first board resolution, including ratification of incorporation, adoption of the registered office, approval of share allotments, and confirmation of officer appointments. Open a New Zealand corporate bank account for the company; complete bank-mandated KYC using the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN, director identification, and beneficial ownership declaration. For the AIGC SaaS business, register merchant accounts with Stripe and Paddle, providing the certificate of incorporation, proof of registered office, director identification, and anticipated monthly turnover. File the annual return and financial statements as required under s 214 of the Companies Act 1993 and the Financial Reporting Act 2013; maintain the share register, director register, and minute book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
Signed pro forma first board resolution (as recorded)
Directors' identification (passport and proof of address) for bank KYC
Company constitution (if adopted)
Bank account opening forms and beneficial ownership schedule
Stripe and Paddle onboarding applications with entity due-diligence pack
Registered office address proof and lease agreement (if any)
Share register and register of directors as required by the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank or payment processor queries the corporate structure or asks for enhanced due diligence, the company should provide a certified organizational chart, a statutory declaration from the sole director confirming non-resident beneficial ownership, and the tax classification statement reflecting the entity's low-risk SaaS profile; the board may pass a curative resolution ratifying any missing authorization prior to resubmission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board applies to a pure software/AIGC video-generation business under ISIC 6201 in New Zealand. The general regulatory authority is the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); however, no manufacturing, industrial, or operational license is triggered by the company's SaaS and virtual-avatar software activities, and the 'requires_statutory_license' flag in the corporate metadata is false.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operational or manufacturing permit is required for the company's activities. The company operates under the general law as a New Zealand registered limited liability company engaged in software publishing (NAICS 511210); optionally, it may hold an internal ISO/IEC 27001 certification or NZ Information Security Registered Assessor Program (NZSAP) attestation for voluntary information-security credibility, but such certification is not a statutory license.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 4 (no physical works, no land disturbance, no discharges to air, land, or water; no 'activity' under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991). A formal Environmental Impact Assessment is not required for an office-based software company whose principal inputs are electricity, computing infrastructure, and cloud data-center services. Any leasing of office premises is subject to the territorial authority building and fire regulations only.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None imposed at formation. Should the company later occupy physical premises, it must comply with the Resource Management Act 1991 general duty under s 15 (no unreasonable noise, discharge of contaminants, or waste) and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for electronic-waste disposal. No wastewater or VOC thresholds apply to the software business; cloud data-center emissions are outside the company's operational discharge profile, but voluntary carbon reporting under the Climate Change Response Act 2002 (ETS exposure only if the company directly operates emitting stationary systems) is not triggered.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company, as a low-risk office-based software employer, must comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 (HSWA): implement a worker engagement and participation system, conduct a simple workplace risk assessment for office ergonomics, and maintain first-aid and emergency-communication arrangements. Any leased premises must hold a current building warrant of fitness issued by the territorial authority under the Building Act 2004, confirming structural, fire-safety (means of escape, smoke detection), and disabled-access compliance. Fire safety is overseen by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ); an evacuation scheme is required only if the premises are classified as 'specified premises' under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. No civil-defense clearance is required for the AIGC software line of business, and no dangerous- or heavy-machinery licenses apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) — statutory tax authority with exclusive national jurisdiction; primary digital administrative portal: myIR (https://www.ird.govt.nz); corporate registration interface: New Zealand Companies Office (https://www.companiesoffice.govt.nz); e-invoicing infrastructure: New Zealand Peppol Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Overseas Company Registration: The CK_IC (a Cook Islands International Company) must be registered as an overseas company under sections 360-363 of the Companies Act 1993 before carrying on business in New Zealand; a New Zealand physical address for service and a registered agent must be appointed; registration automatically issues a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN), which is the primary public identifier. Step 2 — IRD Number (Tax File Number): File an application with the IRD using Form IR596 (Company/International Company Registration) or the corresponding myIR onboarding workflow; provide the NZBN, certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation from the Cook Islands International Companies Act 1984, overseas company registration number, registered office details, full director/ultimate beneficial owner particulars, and a description of the AI avatar video-generation SaaS activities; the IRD issues a 9-digit IRD number, normally within 5-10 business days. Step 3 — GST Registration: Register for GST within myIR once the 12-month rolling value of taxable supplies reaches NZD 60,000 (statutory threshold under section 51, Goods and Services Tax Act 1985), or voluntarily register earlier if the entity carries on a taxable activity; the effective registration date may be backdated to the date liability first arose, subject to IRD discretion. Step 4 — Approved Issuer Status: If the IC will issue debt securities to non-residents, apply for Approved Issuer status (Form IR549) to access the 2% Approved Issuer Levy instead of 15% NRWT on qualifying interest. All registrations are managed through myIR; a dedicated Inland Revenue account is created with electronic filing, notice service, and refund processing capabilities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Non-Resident International Company with Territorial Scope): The CK_IC is a limited-liability corporate entity incorporated in the Cook Islands under the International Companies Act 1984, where offshore income is subject to 0% corporate tax. For New Zealand tax purposes, the company is classified as a non-resident company: it is not incorporated in New Zealand and its centre of management and control is located outside New Zealand (sections YC 2-YC 3, Income Tax Act 2007). As a non-resident, New Zealand taxes the CK_IC on an entity-level basis but strictly on New Zealand-sourced income at the corporate rate of 28%; all foreign-sourced income, including all revenue derived from the AI avatar video-generation SaaS exports to non-resident customers, is exempt under section CW 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007 (foreign-sourced income of non-residents). No pass-through or look-through classification applies to a non-resident corporate vehicle under New Zealand law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; tax classification follows statutory residency (sections YC 2-YC 3, ITA 2007). Available statutory elections and regimes that a CK_IC may utilise include: (1) GST grouping election (sections 55-56, GST Act 1985) — related New Zealand companies may elect to be treated as a single GST group; (2) Approved Issuer Levy election (section 32J, Stamp and Cheque Duties Act 1971) — election by an approved issuer to pay 2% AIL on qualifying interest paid to non-residents in substitution for 15% NRWT; (3) hybrid mismatch ordering and timing elections (Subpart FH, ITA 2007) — allows the IC to align deduction timing and prevent double-dip outcomes under New Zealand's BEPS hybrid rules; (4) Foreign Investment Fund (FIF) elective accounting for resident shareholders, though inapplicable to the non-resident IC itself; (5) election for the GST treatment of cross-border remote services under section 8B of the GST Act 1985 to characterise the AI avatar supply as an export of services eligible for zero-rating.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — value-added tax regime administered by the Inland Revenue Department under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 — taxable supplies in the preceding or current 12-month period (section 51, GST Act 1985); a single taxable supply of NZD 60,000 or more in a 12-month period also triggers mandatory registration; voluntary registration is available where the IC carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand. The CK_IC's B2B export supplies of AI video-generation services are zero-rated and count towards the NZD 60,000 threshold for registration purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or any API-based pre-transaction authorisation. Electronic invoicing is fully recognised and permitted; adoption is voluntary and operates through the New Zealand Peppol Authority's certified access points for interoperable cross-border e-invoicing. Where e-invoices are used, they must satisfy all GST invoice content requirements of section 24 of the GST Act 1985: supplier name and GST registration number, invoice issue date, recipient name and address, quantity and nature of the AI avatar/video-generation services supplied, consideration in New Zealand dollars, and a clear statement that the supply is zero-rated as an export. The IRD conducts post-lodgement risk-based audit and clearance reviews through myIR, with a key audit focus on cross-border digital service exporters.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The CK_IC may claim 0% GST on its exported AI avatar video-generation services under the following cumulative criteria: (a) the supply constitutes a supply of services to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed (section 11A(1)(c), GST Act 1985); (b) for automated/remote services — including cloud-delivered AI video synthesis, virtual avatar generation, and SaaS subscriptions — supplied to non-resident recipients located offshore, the supply qualifies as an export of remote services and is zero-rated; (c) the recipient is not in New Zealand at the time the service is rendered or consumed, and the service is not physically performed in New Zealand; (d) the supply is not made to a person in New Zealand and is not connected with a taxable activity carried on in New Zealand by the recipient; (e) the supplier holds contemporaneous evidentiary material confirming the non-resident status of the recipient, including a foreign tax registration number, geolocation/IP address logs, a registered business address outside New Zealand, and payment instruments originating offshore. The zero-rating applies to B2B and B2C remote digital services provided the recipient and the consumption location are outside New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — lodged via the Trade Single Window / ExDocs system whenever tangible media, server hardware, prototype devices, or embedded components accompany the AI avatar software; not required for pure digital/original-export delivery models

Zero-Rated Tax Invoice — commercial invoice expressly stating 'GST 0% — Export Supply under section 11A(1)(c), GST Act 1985' and containing the IRD's invoice-combination requirements: CK_IC supplier name and GST number, recipient name and offshore address, supply description of the AI avatar video-generation licence, quantum of services, total amount in NZD
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill — mandatory for any physical component of the composite supply; conclusively proves physical exportation and timestamp

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank-issued certificate or SWIFT MT103/MT950 confirmations together with Stripe/Paddle settlement statements evidencing payment originating from offshore customer accounts within the 180-day export settlement cycle

Non-Resident Evidence Pack — overseas company extract or foreign tax registration certificate (e.g., ABN, HMRC VAT number, US state registration), customer's written confirmation of non-resident location, IP-address geolocation records for each supply event, and the executed SaaS subscription/licence agreement governing the AI avatar video-generation services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The IRD treats export zero-rating as a high-risk compliance domain, particularly for digital SaaS exporters using third-party payment rails. If the CK_IC fails to substantiate the non-resident supply or cannot evidence repatriation of forex proceeds within the 180-day acknowledgment window, the IRD will retrospectively reverse the zero-rating and assess output GST at 15% on the full consideration, with Use-of-Money Interest (UOMI) calculated from the original GST return due date. Statutory shortfall penalties are superimposed: 20% for failure to exercise reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for a taxpayer-abuse position, and 150% for evasion (sections 141A-E, Tax Administration Act 1994); penalties are assessed on the GST shortfall plus the primary tax. Criminal prosecution may follow under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994, exposing the CK_IC and its directors to fines up to NZD 100,000 for companies and imprisonment up to 5 years, in addition to a permanent debarment from the NZBN myIR electronic filing concessions. Fraudulent refund claims (e.g., improper zero-rated refund drawings) attract automatic triple-recovery remedies: reinstatement of GST, UOMI, and the 150% evasion penalty, with the IRD empowered to freeze bank accounts and pursue recovery against the New Zealand registered agent and the ultimate beneficial owners under the anti-avoidance and piercing provisions of the Companies Act 1993 and the Tax Administration Act 1994.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ / Te Pūtea Matua), acting as the prudential regulator and operator of the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS) and the NZClear high-value settlement system. Exchange control derived from the Crown's residual foreign-exchange powers under the Public Finance Act 1989, administered in practice through the Overseas Investment Act 2005 by the Overseas Investment Office (OIO) for investment-specific screening, and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 for instruments requiring regulated offer disclosure. For routine trade and SaaS export flows, no RBNZ licence, prior approval, or ministerial consent is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. New Zealand maintains no exchange control regime, no surrender requirements, and no balancing restrictions on the repatriation of dividends, royalties, or loan principal by non-resident investors. Profit remittance hurdles arise exclusively from tax source rules, not FX rules: dividend and royalty payments to a non-resident recipient attract Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at 15% unpaid or 10% under an applicable double tax agreement if the recipient qualifies, and interest can be lowered to 2% via the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL). The Tax-Exempt Zone classification of the International Company does not erase the payer's withholding obligations under sections RF2 and RF8 of the Income Tax Act 2007. Capital inflows from non-resident shareholders are unrestricted unless the investment acquires significant New Zealand business assets, sensitive land, or fishing quota requiring OIO consent under the Overseas Investment Act 2005, which is not triggered by SaaS intellectual property licensing, receivables purchasing, or payment settlement flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines, no mandatory conversion ratios, and no export proceeds surrender obligations under New Zealand law. The International Company may retain 100% of its export earnings in foreign currency and may hold settlement balances in offshore digital platforms (Stripe, Paddle, Wise) without restriction. Foreign-currency receipts are aggregated for Balance of Payments statistical collection by the Reserve Bank and Statistics New Zealand, and a reporting entity whose total annual cross-border turnover exceeds NZD 1 million may be selected for the quarterly BOP enterprise survey; however, completion is a statistical return and does not mandate conversion, deposit, or repatriation timelines. For prudential accounting, export proceeds should be recognised at spot settlement date using RBNZ daily reference rates and matching hedges must be properly designated under the IC's accounting policy to avoid revaluation volatility.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Multi-Currency Operational Account (NZD, USD, EUR, GBP) with segregated Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Operational Treasury Account with Dedicated Escrow Facility and Foreign Currency Settlement Ledger
Transactional Operating Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account with API-enabled clearing
Business Transactional Account with Escrow Sub-Ledgers and SWIFT/LC desk for trade disbursements
Corporate Transaction Account only; limited specialist cross-border treasury suite and no large-volume LC trading desk

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium - Feasibility is conditional on regulated licensing. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Wise, Airwallex, Paddle Treasury, Stripe Treasury) are not registered banks and cannot directly access RBNZ's Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). They may lawfully hold transactional balances for the IC if the EMI is registered on the Financial Service Providers Register (FSPR) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008, or operates through a New Zealand-licensed custodian bank. The IC may use such platforms as a secondary settlement rail for SaaS subscription revenues and vendor payouts below NZD 50,000 per transaction; the primary treasury account, capital escrow, and LC issuance must remain with a registered commercial bank in New Zealand to preserve security, audit opinion, and insolvency remoteness.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: New Zealand imposes no statutory mandate requiring directors to appear physically in the jurisdiction to open a corporate bank account. In practice, Tier-1 banks require remote identity verification through certified true copies of passports, a live video-conference interview with each director and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), and independent verification of residential street addresses that must not be a virtual mailbox or a registered-agent-only address. For the International Company with a Tax-Exempt Zone classification and 100% non-resident ownership, enhanced due diligence is expected: (i) a live interview with the relationship manager and compliance officer; (ii) apostilled or consular-certified passport copies for all directors and UBOs; (iii) a board resolution confirming the authorised signatory matrix; (iv) issuance of the corporate register extract from the Companies Office or equivalent registry; (v) a confirmed New Zealand-based compliance contact (the registered agent of file) who undertakes to maintain records and update KYC; and (vi) potentially the collection of activation tokens or signatory specimen cards at an NZ branch or correspondent bank where the bank's policy requires a physical artifact. Remote onboarding is therefore feasible but not frictionless; a same-week physical visit to Auckland recommended during the first 12 months materially de-risks the banking approval timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership: the International Company is owned through a trust or corporate chain that does not immediately surface a natural person UBO, triggering a Know-Your-Customer failure under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 and the bank's correspondent-bank 'nested due diligence' rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed and deed of adherence; certificate of incorporation; register of beneficial owners; a multi-level corporate chart showing each intermediate entity with jurisdiction of incorporation, company number, registered agent name, and percentage ownership; government-issued passport and proof of residential address for each UBO; a signed source-of-wealth statement attested by the UBO; and a cover letter from the licensed New Zealand agent confirming the UBO list is current.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of initial capital injection: the first inbound equity deposit exceeding NZD 50,000 originates from cryptocurrency exchanges, a token sale, or a foreign trust without auditable fiat provenance, triggering source-of-funds enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the sending financial institution showing the specific fiat wire; audited or reviewed financial statements of the investor entity or trust; the executed token sale or convertible note agreement; crypto-to-fiat exchange withdrawal receipts and order IDs for the exact fiat amount; a shareholder resolution authorising the capital injection; UBO personal net-worth certificate issued by an approved accounting firm; and CRS self-certification or Form W-8BEN-E for any US-connected UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office registered address and absence of substantive physical or economic footprint, causing the bank's financial-crime team to flag a 'registered-office-only shell' profile and the US and EU correspondent banks to subject incoming wires to additional OFAC/FATF screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed services agreement with the New Zealand registered agent; evidence of an engaged New Zealand professional board of advisers (chartered accountant and shipping or IP tax counsel); letter from a New Zealand tax firm confirming the IC's tax status and economic substance expectations; board resolution adopting an economic-substance policy aligned with the actual IP holding and licensing operation; annual accounting and audit arrangements in place with a NZ CPA firm; and a notarised commitment to retain all business records in the registered office premises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and no New Zealand tax residence for beneficial owners: relationship managers question the control nexus, the absence of IRD record prior to onboarding, and the genuineness of the entity's status as a 'tax-exempt zone' international company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IRD taxpayer reference number for the International Company; fully completed IR976 forms for each non-resident director; certificate of tax residence from the director's home revenue authority; New Zealand tax counsel advice confirming that SaaS licensing revenue qualifies as foreign-sourced without an NZ permanent establishment; executed merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe and Paddle demonstrating outsourcing of payment acquisition to regulated worldwide platforms; and the standard-form software-as-a-service terms proving active business operation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Merchant-of-record and SaaS revenue channel ambiguity: inbound revenues from Stripe and Paddle arrive as aggregated settlement pools rather than per-customer invoices, and the bank suspects structured volume or undisclosed third-party settlements rather than genuine user activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant-of-record agreements with both Stripe and Paddle; six months of platform payout statements; export of per-subscription invoices from the billing system generated at the IC's registered name; a documented refund and chargeback policy; RBNZ-mapped business purpose code K200 for software export receipts; a breakdown of revenue by geography; and active user licence metrics demonstrating the underlying AI avatar video generation service is a real commercial product.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing is executed as follows: (1) the shareholder sends a SWIFT MT103 from a regulated foreign financial institution to the IC's designated NZD Capital Escrow sub-account at the chosen Tier-1 bank; the full SWIFT address must be pre-confirmed by the treasury desk (e.g., ANZBNZ22 for ANZ, BKNZNZ22 for BNZ, WPACNZ2W for Westpac); (2) the remitter must populate field 70/Remittance Information with a purpose code of K800 for direct investment equity injection and the beneficiary reference 'CAPESC-IC04' which matches the bank's internal standing instruction; (3) before credit, the bank screens names against OFAC, HM Treasury, EU, UN, and New Zealand Sanctions Registers, and the IC must attach in its onboarding file the source-of-funds dossier described above; (4) for inter-company capital transfers above NZD 500,000, the bank prepares a statistical BOP return to the Reserve Bank, but no OIO consent is required because the SaaS IP and accounts receivable are not sensitive New Zealand assets; (5) allocation instruction: 40% to NZD operating current account, 30% to USD settlement ledger for Stripe payouts, and 30% to a EUR/GBP multi-currency ledger for European disbursements; (6) where the injection is structured as a shareholder loan rather than equity, an executed loan agreement with a fixed maturity, at arm's-length interest rate, and a shareholder resolution must be lodged to distinguish debt from paid-up capital; (7) an optional Fast-Activities path is available for tranches below NZD 10,000 via Wise platform treasury, but the IC must instruct the platform to tag all payments with the same purpose code and maintain a mirror ledger to prevent the bank from reclassifying revenue as undetermined settlement flows.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are segregated by payment size and instrument type: (i) SWIFT MT103 for single supplier invoices exceeding USD 10,000, with the beneficiary bank sorted using the standard NZ clearing directory; (ii) Commercial Letter of Credit at sight for GPU compute, bare-metal cloud infrastructure, colocation hosting, and data-residency vendors, issued by the IC's treasury bank with a maximum maturity of 90 days and margin of 110% of invoice value; (iii) NZClear/ESAS same-day settlement for domestic NZD disbursements including payroll, rent, and professional fees; (iv) automated SWEEP of payout balances from Stripe and Paddle into the IC's multi-currency settlement ledger daily at 08:00 NZST, using the platform's treasury API; (v) weekly cross-currency conversion executed on the bank's FX desk at the prevailing spot rate plus a 15 basis-point forward cover spread; (vi) bulk employee/contractor payroll in NZD via the bank's payment gateway API to expedite batch processing; and (vii) B2B transfer of refund obligations through the same clearing rails, with the IC's treasury policy requiring positive account balance verification before any refund instruction, and chargeback reserves held in a separate non-operational buffer of not less than one month of average refund volume.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: OTC deliverable FX forwards in AUD, NZD, USD, EUR, and GBP with tenors up to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with CSA
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic remittance currencies (e.g., AED, PHP, INR, NGN, IDR) where local regulatory conversion restrictions exist for offshore settlement
FX swaps (spot versus forward) benchmarked to the monthly payout cycles of Stripe and Paddle revenue receipts
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to convert USD-denominated infrastructure loans into NZD floating-rate liabilities tied to SOFR or BKBM equivalent benchmarks
European-style vanilla FX options to establish a maximum cost ceiling for acquisition pipelines and licensed video-synthesis compute purchases
AUD/NZD, EUR/NZD, and GBP/NZD closing-rate forward contracts cleared by the principal bank to eliminate residual settlement mismatch between platform settlement currency and operating currency

Structured forward arrangements over an outright forward with a window feature for event-driven disbursements, permitted only where the underlying exposure arises from a signed SaaS infrastructure service contract

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Register of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's incorporation anniversary each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a late fee of approximately USD 35; continued non-compliance triggers a 20-working-day notice and may result in administrative strike-off or removal from the Companies Register

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for 'large' companies: entities nent NZ$20M in total assets, or nent NZ$50M in annual revenue, or employing 50+ persons, for each of the two preceding consecutive accounting periods; smaller companies may also be required to audit if shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights request one
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand Equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS); reduced disclosure regime (NZ IFRS RDR) and NZ IFRS for SMEs are available for eligible small-to-medium entities

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone UBO filing is required with the Registrar; the annual confirmation updates the complete list of shareholders and directors as of the confirmation date. Every share transfer must be recorded in the company's share register within 10 working days of notification; beneficial-ownership records are maintained internally and disclosed to authorities only where required under the AML/CFT Act 2009

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays exist in New Zealand. Effective preferential reliefs include: (i) the R&D Tax Incentive, a refundable tax credit equal to 15% of eligible R&D expenditure (capped at NZD 50 million per year per group, applicable to software and AI R&D from the 2019-20 income year); (ii) full imputation of corporate tax to resident shareholders, eliminating economic double taxation on distributed profits; (iii) indefinite carry-forward of tax losses (subject to the 49% shareholder continuity or business continuity test) and a one-year loss carry-back of up to NZD 500,000; and (iv) foreign tax credits for foreign income already taxed abroad, which reduce residual NZ tax on cross-border SaaS/royalty revenue streams.
